segments.he: אוּמָּן אֵין לוֹ חֲזָקָה וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַבָּה: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּסַר לוֹ בְּעֵדִים, אֲבָל מָסַר לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בְּעֵדִים – מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁיָּכוֹל לוֹמַר לוֹ ״לֹא הָיוּ דְבָרִים מֵעוֹלָם״, כִּי אָמַר לֵיהּ נָמֵי ״לְקוּחָה הִיא בְּיָדִי״ – מְהֵימַן.
segments.en: § The Gemara returns to discuss the statement of Shmuel (42b): «A craftsman does not have» the ability to establish the «presumption» of ownership of the property in his possession, but a partner has the ability to establish the presumption of ownership. «Rabba says: They taught» this «only» in a case «where» the owner «transferred» the item «to» the craftsman «in» the presence of «witnesses. But» if the owner «transferred» the item «to» the craftsman «not in» the presence of «witnesses,» then, «since» the craftsman «is able to say to» the one who claims to be the owner: «These matters never occurred,» i.e., you did not give me this item but it was mine to begin with, and he would keep possession of the item with that claim, then «even when» the craftsman «says to him: It is purchased» by me from you, and that is why it is «in my possession,» he is «deemed credible.»

moves.about: a craftsman cannot establish presumption of ownership
the rule holds only where the item was handed over before witnesses; otherwise a miggo makes the craftsman credible

positions.claim: without witnesses to the transfer the craftsman is believed that he bought it
positions.basis: miggo: he could have said it never happened
